notes: The 1964 volume of the Recreation and Park Commission. Curated: the Allyne property acquisition, playground and diamond names, and design approvals for Embarcadero Plaza and Storyland.

coverage.remaining: Routine items not curated. Not placed: the Golden Gateway garage park (final plans approved Dec 17, Res 6052; no page), the Zoological Society's African Scene, deer moat and aviary request (Dec 17, sketches by J. Francis Ward; approval not legible), Ernest E. Burden's offer of the Gothic redwood roof of the demolished Seventh Day Adventist church at Geary and Octavia to the Palace of Fine Arts (deferred), the request to name a McLaren Park playground for Commissioner Herz (referred, Jun 11). The $58,590 supplemental appropriation for the Allyne property (Res 5911, Aug 13) is legible only in the index.

findings.address_as_written: Allyne Property, northwest corner of Green and Gough Streets
findings.description: Having recommended in January that the city buy the Allyne property at Green and Gough Streets for a park, the Recreation and Park Commission took the question up again at the Board of Supervisors' request. The National Society of Colonial Dames, owners of the lots next door, pledged $10,000 toward the purchase, and the Citizens Committee to Preserve the Allyne Property, with William W. Wurster as honorary chairman, wrote that the house was of both historic and architectural significance. The Commission agreed to allow six months after the city acquired the land for a group to propose restoring the house and keeping it as a public museum.

findings.description: Told that the preservation committee had withdrawn its interest in the Allyne house, and that the Supervisors' parks committee wanted the property bought strictly as a park and not kept as a museum, the Recreation and Park Commission revoked its six-month offer and resolved that the property be acquired for park purposes only, asking for an official appraisal.
